aria: Animated recap of the Timberwolves' 104 to 95 home win over the Grizzlies: Ayo Dosunmu's driving layup with 21 seconds left in the third quarter that made it 83 to 62, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jaden McDaniels' 25 points, the top scorers, how the Timberwolves won, and Monday's game against the Nets.

notes: Box score from the Minnesota Timberwolves' 104–95 home win over the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday, Nov 21, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, checked player by player against the CBS Sports gametracker box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via myMotherLode and CBS Sports), Field Level Media and the Grizzlies and Timberwolves On SI sites. All 104 Minnesota points and all 95 Memphis points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (28–28–27–21 to 34–12–16–33) add up to both totals: 56–46 Minnesota at the half and 83–62 after three. Team totals (field goals 43 of 74 to 38 of 89, blocks 8–4, steals 8–14), points in the paint (60–52) and the biggest leads (Minnesota 23, Memphis 11) are from the Covers.com box score; AP says Memphis was down 23 early in the fourth and Field Level Media that Memphis led by as many as 11 in the first quarter. Second- and fourth-quarter points are from the line score. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Saturday's games (12–5, 3rd in the West; the Nets 3–12).

Down 11 early in the second quarter, Minnesota went on a 26–6 run capped by a Rudy Gobert dunk off a missed LaMelo Ball free throw and led 56–46 at the half after winning the quarter 28–12 (AP; Field Level Media). Ayo Dosunmu had three driving layups as Minnesota scored 14 of the final 16 points of the third quarter (AP), the last of them with 21 seconds left for 83–62 (Field Level Media). Memphis cut a 23-point deficit to 97–90 on Cedric Coward's three with 2:37 left before Jaden McDaniels answered with back-to-back layups (AP; Field Level Media). McDaniels had 25 on 11-of-17 shooting (box score; Field Level Media), and Minnesota shot a season-high 58% (AP). Anthony Edwards was out injured (AP). Minnesota has won three of four (AP) and eight of its past 10 (Field Level Media); Memphis lost for the first time in six games and for the first time on the road in nine games, with season lows for points in a quarter (12), a half (46) and a game (AP). The Timberwolves host Brooklyn on Monday and the Grizzlies play at Charlotte on Monday (AP).

On Memphis' side, Cedric Coward tied his season high with 23 points (8 of 16, 4 of 7 from three) with 7 rebounds and 4 steals, and Ty Jerome scored 18 in his first game back after missing four with a right hip impingement (box score; AP; Grizzlies On SI). Memphis was without Cam Boozer (right ankle sprain) and Jerami Grant (left calf strain) (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Ayo Dosunmu's layup with 21 seconds left in the third quarter that made it 83–62 (Field Level Media); AP describes his three layups in that closing stretch as driving layups, so it is drawn as a drive, and the score before it is shown as a 19-point margin (a two-point layup). The stories don't give the angle of the drive or the defender. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Minnesota Timberwolves or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Ayo Dosunmu's 2021 draft combine measurements: 6-foot-5 in shoes, 194 pounds and a 6-foot-10.25 wingspan (nbadraft.net). No source we read gave his Minnesota number, so no number is drawn. He is drawn in Minnesota's home white with the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
